recommendation_summary: Act now: keep the current folder for drafts and add a 'Released' folder that only the three reviewers can write to. A reviewer approves by saving the exact file there, ideally as a PDF. A seven-year retention lock blocks edits and deletes, and the platform audit log records who added each file and when. Policy covers one gap: a different reviewer releases any document a reviewer wrote. No optional additions. Unmet needs: the platform is unknown, so retention-lock and audit-log support are unconfirmed. The reply also never ensures the audit log itself is kept for seven years.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The signed customer contract requires, for seven years, the exact approved version, the approver's identity and the approval time; no self-approval; later edits must not alter the approved copy. You need this before this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: Typed initials in an APPROVED column. Any author can type any initials, and authors can edit the folder, so it fails no-self-approval, approver identity and approval time. A naming convention does not stop edits either.
labels.Bottleneck: Write access. Authors can change anything in the shared folder, including what was approved.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you've told me. I haven't seen which platform the folder is on or what retention and permission features it has.

note: The reviewer-only locked folder plus audit log is the right kind of control, but the approval record relies on a platform audit log whose seven-year retention is never secured, and reviewer self-approval is blocked only by policy.
